status: written before the diagnostic defined here ran; the pcf:all arms it explains (MBv2 INT8 -25.3 pp, R18 INT8 -1.3 pp, MBv3 INT8 +1.1 pp) were measured before it
observation_motivating_it: pcf:all (addendum 2) regresses MobileNetV2 INT8 by 25 pp. Candidate mechanism: folding per-input-channel activation scale ratios r_c into a dense consumer's weights before per-output-channel weight quantization moves the channel-range disparity into the weights, so input channels with small r_c get few or zero weight codes.

diagnostic.kind: CPU only, no GPU, no accuracy measured, no new record under artifacts/experiment_b2_attrib/arms
diagnostic.arm: pcf:all (the same per-channel scales as the arm: pcfull on the FP32 activations of the first 256 calibration images; the same fold function engine._fold)
per_folded_consumer: zero weight-code fraction: default per-output-channel MSE weight codes vs folded codes Qw(W r)
silenced input channels: input channels c whose folded codes are zero for every output channel (and the same count for the default codes)
range-weighted relative weight error: ||(W_eff - W) r||_F / ||W r||_F with W_eff = Qw(W) (default) or Qw(W r)/r (folded); r = per-channel scale / per-tensor scale
scale spread log2(max r / min r) of the folded boundary
diagnostic.summary: per model: medians and maxima over folded dense consumers, and the consumers ranked by folded minus default error
diagnostic.reading: the fold mechanism is supported if MobileNetV2 shows much larger folded-weight error growth and silenced input channels than MobileNetV3 and ResNet18; it does not isolate the accuracy effect (no arm), so it is reported as mechanism evidence only

evidence: development (calibration images only; no screen images are evaluated)
